evals.name: empty-args-routes-to-stats-dashboard
evals.expected_output: Empty args route to the stats action (not a missing-action error). Emits the work-item dashboard: open and claimed counts, overdue recurring items, and a category/area breakdown. Read-only — creates or modifies nothing.
expectations: Routes empty `$ARGUMENTS` to the `stats` action — does NOT error on a missing/unknown action
Reports both open-item and claimed-item counts
Surfaces recurring items past their `next_due` date (overdue)
Includes a category/area breakdown of open work
Performs no write — no item created, closed, labeled, or assigned

evals.name: work-auto-selects-one-item-via-seam-claim
evals.expected_output: Reclaims stale leases at session start (idempotent), auto-selects exactly ONE item from the frontier (open, unblocked, unassigned) via the seam list-frontier, then acquires it through the seam claim verb (assignee + lease record, race-safe) before executing it via the full 8-step workflow. The claim identity is the authenticated session user, never the bot.
expectations: Runs an idempotent session-start reclaim (`work-item-tracker.sh reclaim`) before selecting — never releases a live lease
Selects exactly ONE item to work — never claims multiple at once
Selects from the frontier via `work-item-tracker.sh list-frontier` (open, `blocked_by_count == 0`, unassigned); `--autonomous` additionally excludes `needs-human`
Acquires via the seam `work-item-tracker.sh claim` (assignee + lease comment, same-identity aware) — NOT a `status:considering`/`status:claimed` label hold protocol
On a lost race (`claim` exit 7) advances to the next candidate rather than retrying the same item
Executes the selected item through the 8-step workflow (/explore -> /research -> /architect -> /implement -> /test-plan -> /quality-gate -> /verify-changes outcome -> /retro)

evals.name: decompose-vertical-slices-hitl-afk-dependency-order
evals.expected_output: Reads the source (default: the topic's PLAN.md phases via the two-location lookup — docs/topics/<slug>/PLAN.md contract slice, then .work/<slug>/PLAN.md under contract_tier: local), drafts thin tracer-bullet vertical slices cutting through all layers, classifies each AFK (labeled agent-ready) vs HITL (labeled needs-human), orders by dependency, gets user approval, then publishes blockers-first via the seam create-item with native --blocked-by edges without touching the parent item.
expectations: Drafts VERTICAL tracer-bullet slices (each a complete end-to-end path through all layers), NOT horizontal single-layer slices

Classifies each slice AFK (`agent-ready` label) vs HITL (`needs-human` label — the label `list-frontier --autonomous` honors to exclude an item from autonomous pickup; omitting `agent-ready` alone does NOT); prefers AFK, marks HITL only for genuine human-judgment / design-review / manual-QA needs
Presents the breakdown for approval with per-slice Type + Blocked-by + scope, iterating one question at a time with the user before creating anything
Publishes items in dependency order (blockers first) via `work-item-tracker.sh create-item`, recording dependencies as native `--blocked-by` edges
Does NOT close or modify the parent item

evals.name: triage-routes-unsolicited-pr-as-item-with-attached-code
evals.prompt: /work-items:work-items triage 88 — #88 is a pull request from an outside contributor we never asked for, adding a caching layer
evals.expected_output: Routes to the triage action and runs the unsolicited PR through the same raw-intake state machine as an issue (raw -> verified -> briefed -> autonomous-eligible). Treats the diff as an attachment to evaluate — checks it out and runs the relevant tests to confirm it does what it claims — never as an obligation to merge. Recommends bug-vs-enhancement classification and a target state, and waits for user direction before mutating anything.
expectations: Routes `triage 88` to the triage action and accepts a PR number — a PR is an item with attached code, entering the same intake as an issue
Evaluates the diff as an attachment (check out, run relevant tests) rather than treating the PR as an obligation to merge
Classifies the request bug vs enhancement (Type `Bug` vs `Feature`) before recommending a state
Recommends and waits for user direction before applying labels, commenting, or closing
Routes any label/comment/close writes through the bound adapter's mechanics and any item creation through the seam `create-item` — no inline provider commands

evals.name: triage-verifies-bug-before-interviewing
evals.prompt: /work-items:work-items triage 17 — #17 is an external bug report claiming exports silently drop rows; the description is thin
evals.expected_output: Attempts to reproduce the reported failure from the reporter's steps BEFORE asking the reporter or user any questions about the fix. On confirmed reproduction the item becomes verified and the brief gets stronger; on failure or insufficient detail it applies status:needs-info with a structured comment preserving what was established so far, rather than interviewing about an unconfirmed claim.
expectations: Attempts reproduction of the reported failure BEFORE any interview — never asks about the fix for a claim nobody has confirmed
Reports the verification result explicitly: confirmed (with observed behavior), failed, or insufficient detail
On insufficient detail applies `status:needs-info` with the structured template (established-so-far + specific actionable questions), not a bare 'please provide more info'
A briefed outcome follows durability-over-precision: behavioral contracts and named interfaces, no file paths or line numbers, per the agent-brief reference
Applies the autonomous-eligible role label (default `agent-ready`) only after the item is both verified and briefed

evals.name: triage-never-reprocesses-decompose-output
evals.prompt: /work-items:work-items triage 53 — #53 was created last week by /work-items:work-items decompose from our approved PLAN.md
evals.expected_output: Declines to re-triage: items published by decompose are born triaged — classified, role-labeled, and briefed at creation — and never re-enter the intake flow. Explains that triage covers raw intake only (items the team did not author) and points at the item's existing role label/brief instead of re-running the state machine.
expectations: Does NOT re-run the triage state machine on a decompose-published item — such items are born triaged (classified, role-labeled, briefed at creation)
States the exclusion rule: triage covers raw intake only — items the team did not author
Performs no triage writes on the item — no label changes, no needs-info comment, no close
Notes the attention view excludes decompose output by construction (born-labeled items never land in the unlabeled or needs-triage buckets)

evals.name: due-resolves-remapped-recurring-role-before-listing
evals.prompt:
/work-items:work-items due

The tracker binding maps recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep. There are open scheduled-upkeep items, but no label named recurring.
evals.expected_output: At action entry, the due flow reads .work-item-tracker.json, resolves recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep, and uses that exact label in its open-item listing before exact-title reconciliation. It never queries --label recurring and therefore does not misreport existing maintenance items as orphaned.
expectations: Reads config.role_labels[recurring-maintenance] before the first tracker query
Lists open items with the resolved scheduled-upkeep label rather than the default recurring literal
Still exact-matches the full [Maintenance] title after label filtering
Does not report an existing remapped maintenance item as orphaned

evals.name: work-excludes-and-cross-references-remapped-recurring-role
evals.prompt:
/work-items:work-items work

The tracker binding maps recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep. Both due maintenance and ordinary frontier items exist.
evals.expected_output: The work flow resolves recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep before selection. It excludes scheduled-upkeep items from the non-recurring frontier tiers and uses scheduled-upkeep when listing open items for the recurring tiers. It never compares against or queries the default recurring literal.
expectations: Resolves the recurring-maintenance label before any tracker read
Excludes items carrying scheduled-upkeep from non-recurring frontier tiers
Uses --label scheduled-upkeep when cross-referencing recurring candidates
Does not fall back to the recurring literal after a valid remap

evals.name: recheck-closes-remapped-recurring-item
evals.prompt:
/work-items:work-items recheck dependency-review

The tracker binding maps recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep, and the associated open item carries only scheduled-upkeep.
evals.expected_output: The recheck flow resolves recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep at action entry, updates the matched schedule row, searches open items with label:scheduled-upkeep plus the maintenance title, exact-filters the result, and closes the correct item. It never searches label:recurring.
expectations: Resolves the recurring-maintenance role before searching tracker items
Searches with label:scheduled-upkeep rather than label:recurring
Exact-matches the full [Maintenance] title before closing
Updates only the matched schedule row and closes only its associated item

evals.name: audit-detects-orphans-under-remapped-recurring-role
evals.prompt:
/work-items:work-items audit

The tracker binding maps recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep. Existing maintenance items use that label exclusively.
evals.expected_output: The audit resolves recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep before tracker reads and uses --label scheduled-upkeep for orphan reconciliation. Existing maintenance items remain visible, so the audit does not produce false orphan findings from an obsolete recurring query.
expectations: Resolves the recurring-maintenance role at audit entry
Lists recurring items with the resolved scheduled-upkeep label
Does not query the default recurring literal after the remap
Does not falsely flag schedule entries whose remapped open items exist
